recipes.name: Garlic-Ginger Chicken Wings
ingredients_raw: 5 pounds chicken wings, separated at joints, tips discarded
3 tablespoons hot sauce (such as Frank's Red Hot ®)
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Line 2 baking sheets with aluminum foil; coat with cooking spray.
Season chicken wings with hot sauce, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add vegetable oil; toss to coat.

Place wings and flour in a large, food-safe plastic bag; hold closed tightly and shake until wings entirely coated, no wet spots should remain. Transfer wings to the prepared baking sheets, making sure no wings touch one another. Coat wings with cooking spray.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes; flip wings. Continue baking until wings crispy and no longer pink in the center, about 30 minutes more.
Whisk rice wine vinegar, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, chili paste, and soy sauce together in a saucepan; bring to a boil, then immediately remove from heat.

Toss 1/2 wings and 1/2 glaze together in a large bowl using tongs until evenly coated; transfer to a serving platter. Let sit about 5 minutes to allow glaze to soak into wings before serving. Repeat with remaining wings and glaze.

raw_recipe.headline: Garlic-Ginger Chicken Wings
raw_recipe.description: A deliciously sticky, ginger, and garlic glaze coats baked chicken wings in this easy recipe from Chef John that's perfect for football snacks.

review.reviewBody: These wings were beautiful looking and perfect for guests. Really easy to make. Mine did not stick to the pan, but I also used a lot of vegetable spray. I also used dried garlic pieces and some ginger powder in the glaze since that's what I had. I put some extra garlic powder in the flour as well. To make them look great, let the glaze boil and throw the wings in the pan while it boils, a few at a time, so that the glaze coats the wings. This does not take long - 3 minutes or so. I also put the wings back in the oven for five minutes to kind of seal the sauce in, but this is really not necessary. If you do this, you will have Showpiece wings. I have made these three times now and people raved over them.

The first time I made these I stuck to the recipe (more or less) and got great reviews from wing lovers in my family. However, the last time I made them, I put the wings in the sauce to marinade and didn't coat them with flour. I baked them in the oven with the sauce, turning a few times during the cook. I used two tbls Chilula hot sauce and then added Chou Chili Sauce (one heaping tablespoon to 12 lbs of wings). I let them marinade for an hour and then put them in the oven in a single layer, spraying them with cooking oil on top. They turned out delicious. Cutting out the flour step also cut out some carbs.

I used sriracha for the hot sauce. I did cook the wings on my propane grill .....gave a deep smoky flavor and gave the wings a light oil spray to help brown the flour coating.....the sauce was great on my cooked wings ....we honestly couldn't stop eating them....unfortunately I have no leftovers......sigh

We really didn't like the seasonings on the chicken wings at all. I halved the hot sauce since I don't like things that are super hot and it was still too spicy and more importantly too vinegar-y. There wasn't a lot of flavor to them. The sauce smelled terrible but tasted very good, it just needs a different spice base for the chicken. If we make the sauce again I would increase the Thai chili sauce slightly and decrease the rice vinegar a bit. 

One thing I did that worked very well was to put the wings on parchment paper instead of foil. I still sprayed the mwith the cooking spray, and when I turned them I put them on a different spot on the parchment paper. Nothing stuck so that was a win.

These wings are EXCELLENT! I prepared half the recipe as we are not too many. I must say that the sauce is worthy of all the stars. I would say that you can prepare it as dipping sauce for other items such as spring rolls. Anyway, I followed the recipe as is except that I cooked the garlic and ginger in a dab of vegetable oil as I can't eat them raw. I must say that it was so aromatic and delicious. OH! More important I had no red sauce or chili sauce (can't eat them). I used buffalo wings sauce. I thought it would ruin the sauce but hat to take the plunge as I can't eat red pepper based spicy sauces. LO and BEHOLD THIS WAS BEYOND DELICIOUS AND THE PERFECT MILDNESS for my sensitive stomach!!!! These are show stopper wings! I would recommend using non-stick aluminum foil and spray the oil over the wings and pan as well.

This turned out wonderful! For the sticking issue I used non-stick aluminum foil and coated it generously with cooking spray and I had minimal sticking. I also went along with recommendations by putting the sauce on the chicken for the last 10 minutes of baking and used extra chili sauce for that kick. Great with carrots and celery!

I didn't have any rice wine vinegar so I substituted apple cider vinegar. I also added 2 tablespoons of teriyaki sauce. Baked for 30 minutes on the first side, turned them, applied more cooking spray and baked them for another 20 minutes (cutting the total cooking time by 10 minutes). The chicken was fully cooked and still juicy, while the breading was crispy. My husband is a huge chicken wing fan. He said these are the best wings he's ever had!

DELISH!!! I've made this about 5 times so far nd it never fades. I add about 1/4 cup more brown sugar and lots of extra garlic. Instead of pouring the sauce over the chicken I leave the sauce on simmer, dip the chicken into the sauce and put it back in the oven for about 5 min. DELISH!!!

I followed the recipe exactly except that I used white wine vinegar instead of rice vinegar. I simmered the sauce for probably 20 minutes to thicken it. Tastes alot like a very spicy, very sweet General Tso sauce. Next time I'll cut the sugar in half, maybe add sesame seeds.

My husband and I loved these. I had to adjust the recipe because I only had 2 pounds of wings so I had to wing it LOL. I also substituted almond flour for the flour to make it more keto like. I didn’t have the Asian chili so I substituted Sriracha and when I tossed them in the sauce I put them back in the oven for a few minutes. And when we served them some of the yummy goodness from the floor coating was on the pan so we just scraped it off and put it on our plates with the wings. Not visually appealing but finger licking good! Definitely will make them again.

I was skeptical because the glaze seemed so thin, but the wings absorbed it right up after a few minutes of resting and tossing. I cooked these in my deep fryer (360F 12-13 minutes) so I skipped the cooking spray steps but otherwise pretty closely followed. My one regret was that I shouldn't have done the initial hot sauce step because the ingredients of the sauce made the skin go a touch towards burnt in the fryer. Next time I would just toss the dry wings in seasoned flour, fry, and toss in the delicious glaze.

Wow, I really liked the flavor of these wings. I couldn't find an Asian chili paste so I ended up using the equivalent amount of sirracha sauce. The tangy flavor from the rice wine vinegar was my favorite thing about it.
It was a little to sweet for my liking, next time ill use half the sugar
This is second time I make buffalo chicken wing. I love wings but where I live has no good wings. Thank you Chef John

The best formula for great wings .. hands down .. I cook a lot .. and folks ask me to make “those wings “ again and again I measure accurately .. I do not frig with any changes to the formula .. it is “spot on” Do your self a favour .. get the authorized ingredients Chef John and Team have created and treat yourself or your family and friends .. to the last recipe for wings you will ever need Be well ..
Pretty Good, not far from my original wings (never added flour to bake before) the glazes can vary to present options. I love it!
Gawdddd I love these. Making it third time so far. These chicken wings recipe will be a constant in my kitchen. TY
I have made this recipe several times throughout the years, and it turns out great every time.......
Better than 5 stars !!!
We have had this dish several times. Easy to make and very good.
